name: Hydrogen azide
aliases: HN3, [NNNH], azoimid, azoimide, HN₃, hydrazoic acid, N3H, triazoic acid
summary: Hydrazoic acid, also known as hydrogen azide or azoimide, is a compound with the chemical formula HN3. It is a colorless, volatile, and explosive liquid at room temperature and pressure. It is a compound of nitrogen and hydrogen, and is therefore a pnictogen hydride. It was first isolated in 1890 by Theodor Curtius.
